How to Apply
Applying to the
Graduate School
The next step in your academic and professional journey is right at your fingertips. Apply today to advance your career with a master’s, doctoral, or professional degree from Rutgers–Camden. Join graduate and professional students from around the globe, immerse yourself in groundbreaking research, create lasting works of art, and forge connections with our esteemed faculty.

Access the Application Portal
Start or complete your application online. Be prepared by downloading a sample application to review the questions in the online form.
Let’s get started! In this episode of the Recording Rutgers Podcast, Erick Watt-Udogu, Assistant Dean, and Nadia Agarrat, Assistant Director of Graduate and International Admissions, share tips and resources for navigating the Rutgers University-Camden graduate admissions process. They cover admissions criteria, workshops, and support to help prospective students create strong applications.
Helpful Hints Before You Apply
Be prepared by downloading a sample application to review the questions in the online form.
Identify Requirements
Identify your program of study and requirements for application completion. While you have the option to apply to multiple programs, please be aware that you must finish and submit your initial application before applying to a second program.
Request Transcripts
Request transcript(s) from institutions you’ve attended, including Rutgers. Your institution(s) should send original, official transcripts that display your awarded degree to the admissions office located on the Rutgerg-Camden campus.
Submit Test Scores
You must request your official test scores. When you take the GRE and TOEFL, you will have the option to specify schools to receive your scores. Use institution code 2790 to send your scores to Rutgers. Rutgers does not use ETS department codes.
Contact Recommenders
During the application, you will provide us with the email addresses of the people who will write your recommendations. Contact your recommenders in advance to let them know that they will receive an email from Rutgers-Camden requesting that they submit the recommendation online.
Prepare Your Statement
Compose a personal statement or statement of purpose for your application. Emphasize your academic and career objectives, pertinent experiences, and why you’re a strong match for the program. Articulate your ambitions and their resonance with our community’s values and goals.
Select a Writing Sample
If applicable, select your writing sample prior to applying for graduate school at Rutgers-Camden. Ensure it showcases your best writing and aligns with the program’s requirements. Be attentive to specific guidelines and submit a compelling representation of your abilities.
Frequently Asked Questions
Contact Us
Who do I contact for more information?
For academic inquiries, please consult the Graduate Program Director for your program of interest. For other questions, feel free to contact the Assistant Dean.
Can I call or stop by your office?
Certainly, we encourage you to contact us. Pay us a visit at our office, give us a call, send an email, or connect with us on social media. We’re eager to engage with you.
Application Fees
How much is the application fee?
After you submit your application, you will be required to pay the $70 nonrefundable application fee. We recommend that you make the payment online using a credit card or e-Check through our secure, encrypted website.
Can I pay the application fee later?
Your application will not be reviewed until we have processed your fee payment. You can pay the application fee at a later date by logging back into your application portal.
How do I request an application fee waiver?
Fee waivers are only granted in specific cases outlined below, and deferments are considered under extraordinary circumstances. Requests are reviewed exclusively for applications that are fully submitted and complete.
Automatic Fee Waiver Policy
Rutgers Alumni: Alumni from any Rutgers campus are automatically eligible for an application fee waiver.
U.S. Military Service Members and Veterans: Applicants currently serving in the U.S. Military or Veterans using GI Bill benefits automatically qualify for an application fee waiver.
Requesting an Application Fee Waiver or Deferral
To request a fee waiver or deferral, send an email to Assistant Dean Erick Watt-Udogu that includes:
Important: Applications missing the following information will not be reviewed.
Your application number.
A screenshot of your application checklist showing your application is complete except for the application fee.
If requesting a fee deferral, a statement of need and supporting evidence, such as tax returns or a letter from your financial aid officer.
A brief statement acknowledging the cost of attendance as outlined on the Tuition and Fees page and an outline of how you plan to address these costs (e.g., scholarships, assistantships, or other funding sources).

Working on Your Application
What are the application deadlines?
Submit early for full consideration. Priority for admission decisions and funding is given to applications completed before the posted deadlines. Waiting until the deadline may limit access to funding and available seats. Applications received after deadlines are reviewed only as space and budget allow. Questions about timing or current availability can be directed to the Graduate School contact page.

How do I apply?
You can apply online using the application portal. Rutgers uses a secure, online application with high-grade encryption to protect your information and requires an updated browser with cookies and JavaScript enabled.
Do you work with agents or ambassadors to complete an application?
We have created an application process and resources that are designed to help you to complete the application independently. However, if you have questions about completing any section of the application, we have staff and ambassadors available to assist you at no charge. Please be cautious of agents or individuals who claim to guarantee admission, housing, scholarships, or employment for a fee as the university does not share any student personal or contact information with third parties. Confirm the legitimacy of their connection with the university by reaching out to the Graduate School.
What is an RUID?
Your RUID, a nine-digit number in the following format: ###00####, is emailed to you within 24 to 48 hours after you submit your application.
While your RUID is not used for the application process, you will need it if you decide to enroll and will have the same RUID for your entire history with Rutgers.
If for some reason you have not received your RUID, or have misplaced it, contact us.
How do I resume a saved application?
Log back into the application portal to resume a saved application.
After I submit an application, can I change it?
You cannot change your application after it has been submitted. If you need to make a change or correction to your application, send it in writing to the Assistant Dean.
Checking Your Application Status
When will I receive a decision?
Admissions decisions are made by individual committees, and this process may span several months. We acknowledge your desire for prompt decisions, especially when you’re considering offers from other institutions. If you’re aware that your application is complete, please feel free to reach out to us for an update.
How do I check the status of my application?
Revisiting your application portal offers you the fastest way to stay informed about your application’s progress, including your admissions decision. Check for updates on your recommendations, scores, and transcripts, and conveniently accept or decline your admission offer online.
Our records are regularly updated as we receive and process new information. You can log in as frequently as needed to monitor your application status.
What should I do if I am missing letters of recommendation?
Recommendations should be submitted electronically. If the application portal indicates that your recommendations have not been received, you can resend the emails to your recommenders by clicking on the ‘Resend Form’ button in the Recommendations section of the application.
If your recommender encounters issues with electronic submission, if you require an additional recommendation, or if you need to change a recommender, please contact the Assistant Dean.
What should I do if my test scores are not marked as being received?
If youdo not see your scores listed two weeks after submission, please contact the Assistant Dean.
